segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: הַלּוֹקֵחַ בְּהֵמָה מְנִיקָה מִן הַגּוֹי — אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין שֶׁמָּא בְּנָהּ שֶׁל אַחֶרֶת הָיָה. נִכְנָס לְתוֹךְ עֶדְרוֹ וְרָאָה אֶת הַמַּבְכִּירוֹת מְנִיקוֹת, וְשֶׁאֵינָן מַבְכִּירוֹת מְנִיקוֹת — אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין שֶׁמָּא בְּנָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל זוֹ, אוֹ שֶׁמָּא בְּנָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ בָּא לוֹ אֵצֶל זוֹ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:» In the case of «one who purchases a nursing» female «animal from a gentile, he» does «not» need «to be concerned,» i.e., take into account the possibility, that «perhaps it was» nursing «the offspring of another» animal. Rather, the buyer may assume it had previously given birth. In the case of one who «enters amid his flock and sees» mother animals «that gave birth for the first time» that were «nursing, and» also sees mother animals «that gave birth not for the first time» that were also «nursing, he» does «not» need «to be concerned» that «perhaps the offspring of this» animal «came to that» animal to be nursed, or that «perhaps the offspring of that» animal «came to this» animal to be nursed.

moves.summary: A nursing animal bought from a gentile is presumed to have given birth
In a flock, no concern that young were switched between first-time and experienced mothers

positions.claim: no concern that a nursing animal nurses another's young; each young follows its mother
